definition: In Parkinson’s disease, apathy syndrome refers to clinically significant apathy, meaning reduced motivation or interest as a clinical feature. In the source packet, it usually appeared together with depression and/or anxiety, while a “pure” form without those mood symptoms was rare and showed no distinct cognitive profile.

reasons: The packet supports apathy as a clinically significant feature in Parkinson’s disease, but it does not define apathy as “reduced motivation or interest”; that wording is unsupported by the source packet.
The summary of the study findings is broadly supported, but the definition goes beyond the packet by turning a study result into a general definitional gloss for “apathy syndrome.”
The definition claims that “clinically significant apathy” means “reduced motivation or interest,” but the packet does not provide that meaning/definition of apathy.

While the packet supports that clinically significant apathy in Parkinson’s disease nearly always co-presented with depression and/or anxiety and that “pure” apathy was very rare (2.8%), it does not support the additional phrasing that it “showed no distinct cognitive profile” in the specific way stated (the packet says apathy greatly overlaps with depression/anxiety and suggests apathy may be an epiphenomenon, with “no specific neuropsychological features,” but it does not directly support the exact wording about cognitive profile. )
